mainTopic: A first בעילה on שבת and יום טוב, and the wedding ברכה for an אלמנה
overview: This amud finishes a proof from opening an abscess on שבת. The גמרא rejects it: pus in an abscess is fully separated from the body, but the blood of בתולים is not. Next come practical rulings. רבי אמי, רב זביד and רב יהודה all allowed a first בעילה, and רבא's view on שבת is reported in two opposite versions. רב פפא's version, which forbids it on שבת, leads to a debate about which מלאכות are allowed on יום טוב. Incense is excluded, and a deer is included, because only things every person needs are allowed. רבי יוחנן forbade a first בעילה on שבת, but the final הלכה is that it is permitted. The amud then turns to ברכת חתנים for an אלמנה. A בחור who marries her says the ברכה for seven days, and an אלמון who marries her says it for one day. Three days of rejoicing are a separate count from the days of ברכה.

steps.title: End of the proof from opening an abscess
steps.stepSummary: The last word of a quoted rule: someone who opens an abscess on שבת to let out pus is פטור. This was brought as a proof that a first בעילה should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: …he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: This word finishes a proof the גמרא started just before. Someone who opens an abscess on שבת only to drain the pus is פטור, which here means it is fully allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof compares the two cases. Releasing pus from an abscess is allowed, so releasing the blood of בתולים should be allowed too. The next step will challenge this comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt. Here it means fully permitted, not just 'no punishment'.
An abscess, a pocket of pus. This is the case being finished here.
Pus or fluid that is drained from the abscess.

steps.confusionAlert: Usually פטור on שבת means 'not punished, but still forbidden.' In this case it means completely permitted. That is why it could work as a proof for allowing a first בעילה.

phrases.english: he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof that began before this part of the daf.
steps.raayaObject: That a first בעילה on שבת should be permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that draining pus from an abscess on שבת is פטור (fully permitted).

steps.title: The abscess is different: its pus is fully separated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Pus in an abscess is gathered and fully detached from the body. The blood of בתולים is gathered but not detached.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is gathered and detached. Here, it is gathered but not detached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if we hold that the blood of בתולים is gathered in one spot (דם מפקד פקיד), it is still not fully detached from the body. Pus in an abscess is already completely separate. Letting out the pus removes nothing that is attached, but releasing the blood does pull out something still connected, which is like a forbidden מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Stored or gathered in one place.

phrases.english: There, it is gathered and detached.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the abscess. Its pus is already fully separate from the body.

phrases.english: Here, it is gathered but not detached.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, פְּקִיד וַעֲקִיר. הָכָא, פְּקִיד וְלָא עֲקִיר.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1 by showing the two cases are different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the abscess and בעילה. It does not decide the whole question of first בעילה on שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The abscess's pus is both gathered and detached. The blood of בתולים is gathered but still attached, so the cases are not alike.

steps.title: רבי אמי allows a first בעילה on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבי אמי ruled in practice that a first בעילה is allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי permitted a first-time בעילה on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from theory to practice. It reports that רבי אמי allowed a first בעילה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the proof was rejected, real rulings show that many אמוראים allowed it. This sets up the רבנן's question about the כתובה in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: For the first time (the first בעילה of a בתולה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami permitted
to have relations for the first time on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: 'For the first time' means the first בעילה with a בתולה, the case the whole discussion is about.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי שְׁרָא לְמִיבְעַל בַּתְּחִלָּה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a series of practical rulings on the topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A first בעילה is permitted on שבת.

steps.title: The רבנן object: her כתובה is not written yet
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge רבי אמי. On שבת no כתובה can be written, and living with a wife without a כתובה is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to him: But her כתובה is not written!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן raise a problem with רבי אמי's ruling. The problem has nothing to do with the שבת issue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man may not live with his wife without a כתובה. On שבת the כתובה cannot be written, so it seems the בעילה should not happen. The challenge is about the marriage document, not about מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! An opening word for a challenge.
The marriage contract that guarantees the wife's payment.

phrases.english: The Sages said to him:
But her marriage contract is not written!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: וְהָא לָא כְּתִיבָא כְּתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's ruling from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's permission for a first בעילה on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man may not live with his wife without a כתובה, and a כתובה cannot be written on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אמי: let her hold movable property
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that the wife can take hold of the husband's movable items worth her כתובה. These act as security until the כתובה is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Have her take hold of movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the רבנן. Instead of a written כתובה, she takes movable property as security.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal of a כתובה is to make sure her payment is protected. Giving her valuable items to hold does the same job until the document can be written after שבת. So the problem is solved and the ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Have her seize or take hold of.
Movable property (things you can pick up and carry).

phrases.english: He said to them:
Have her seize movable property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אַתְפְּסוּהָ מִטַּלְטְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical solution: a replacement for the written document
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a written כתובה, a first בעילה on שבת seems impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Movable property held as security takes the place of the כתובה for now, so the בעילה is permitted.

steps.title: רב זביד allows it too, and maybe did it himself
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד also allowed a first בעילה on שבת. Another version says he did it himself on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד permitted a first בעילה on שבת. Some say: רב זביד himself had a first בעילה on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another אמורא who allowed it. It gives two versions of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version רב זביד ruled for others. In the second version he actually did it himself. Acting on a ruling yourself shows even more clearly that you hold it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say. It introduces another version.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid permitted
to have relations for the first time on Shabbat.
There are those who say:
Rav Zevid himself had relations
for the first time on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד שְׁרָא לְמִיבְעַל בַּתְּחִלָּה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another practical ruling like רבי אמי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A first בעילה is permitted on שבת. By one version רב זביד acted on this himself.

steps.title: רב יהודה allows it on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה allowed a first בעילה on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה permitted a first בעילה on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports רב יהודה's ruling, which mentions only יום טוב. This sets up the next step, which explains what the ruling means for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many things are allowed on יום טוב but forbidden on שבת. So someone might think this ruling was limited to יום טוב. The next step deals with that question.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda permitted
to have relations for the first time on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה שְׁרָא לְמִיבְעַל בַּתְּחִלָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling about יום טוב after the rulings about שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A first בעילה is permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: The same is true on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי in the name of רבא explains that רב יהודה's ruling does not mean שבת is forbidden. It is allowed on שבת too. רב יהודה said יום טוב only because that is when the actual case happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: Do not say that it is permitted on יום טוב but forbidden on שבת. The same is true, that it is permitted even on שבת. The case that happened just happened that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי, quoting רבא, warns us not to draw the wrong conclusion from רב יהודה's words. A first בעילה is allowed on שבת as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think רב יהודה mentioned יום טוב on purpose to leave out שבת. רבא says no. The real question he was asked happened on יום טוב, so that is the day he named. This ties רב יהודה in with רבי אמי and רב זביד.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say. It warns against a mistaken conclusion.
The case that happened happened that way. The detail comes from the real event, not from a limit in the law.

steps.whatToRemember: In רב פפי's version of רבא, a first בעילה is permitted on both שבת and יום טוב, and the mention of יום טוב in רב יהודה's ruling is only a detail of the real event. The next step brings רב פפא's opposite version.
steps.confusionAlert: This is only one report of רבא's view. In step 9 רב פפא reports רבא as reading רב יהודה's ruling as permitting only on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common rule for reading rulings: a detail may come from the real story and not set a limit on the law.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
Do not say: on a Festival it is permitted,
but on Shabbat it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is the wrong conclusion רבא is warning against.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת נָמֵי שְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: for the same is true that even on Shabbat it is also permitted,
and the incident that happened, happened this way.
phrases.notes: He means the question רב יהודה was asked came up on a יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב דִּשְׁרֵי, הָא בְּשַׁבָּת אֲסִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the scope of רב יהודה's ruling in step 7 and blocks a wrong conclusion from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A first בעילה is permitted on שבת as well as on יום טוב. רב יהודה named יום טוב only because the real case happened then.

steps.title: A second version: allowed on יום טוב, forbidden on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, quoting רבא, says רב יהודה's ruling means a first בעילה is allowed on יום טוב but forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: on יום טוב it is permitted, on שבת it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of what רבא said about רב יהודה's ruling. This version reads רב יהודה's words exactly: יום טוב only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, רב פפי reported that רבא said שבת is also allowed and יום טוב was just the case that came up. רב פפא reports the opposite: the mention of יום טוב was deliberate, and שבת is forbidden. So there is a real difference between the two days.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב פפי (step 8) and רב פפא (here). They have almost the same name but report opposite versions of רבא.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
On יום טוב it is permitted, on Shabbat it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: He is explaining רב יהודה's ruling from step 7, but reading it the opposite way from step 8.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבא's explanation, which goes against the version in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A first בעילה is allowed on יום טוב and forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: If wounding is allowed on יום טוב, then incense should be too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי asks רב פפא: are you saying that since wounding is allowed on יום טוב for food, it is allowed even without that need? If so, incense should also be allowed on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said to רב פפא: What is your reasoning? Since wounding was allowed for a need, it is allowed even without a need? If so, making incense should be allowed on יום טוב, since lighting fire was allowed for a need, so it should be allowed even without a need!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי guesses the reason behind רב פפא's version and attacks it with a case that is clearly forbidden: burning incense on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, causing a wound is allowed when slaughtering for food. The suggested logic is מתוך: once something is allowed for a need, it is allowed even without that need, which would cover a first בעילה. But the same logic would allow lighting fire for incense, and that is forbidden. So the reasoning seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': once a מלאכה is allowed on יום טוב for a need, it is allowed even without that need
Making a wound that draws blood
Incense: spices put on hot coals to give a nice smell
'But if so': opens a challenge showing a problem with the reasoning

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פַּפִּי לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Pappi said to Rav Pappa:
What is your thinking?
Since making a wound was permitted for a need,
phrases.notes: Slaughtering an animal for יום טוב food makes a wound, and a first בעילה also draws blood.

phrases.english: it was also permitted not for a need?
But if so,
it should be permitted to make incense on יום טוב,
since lighting fire was permitted for a need,
it was also permitted not for a need!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פַּפִּי לְרַב פָּפָּא מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning behind רב פפא's version in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason רב פפא allows a first בעילה on יום טוב: the מתוך principle applied to wounding.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the מתוך principle allows wounding with no food need, it should also allow lighting fire for incense, but incense is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: Only things shared by every person are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק limits יום טוב מלאכה to things that are 'equal for every person'. Incense is not like that, but a first בעילה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About your point, the פסוק says: 'Only what is eaten by every person', meaning something that is equal for every person.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer accepts the מתוך logic but adds a limit taken from a פסוק. That limit leaves out incense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לכל נפש' teach that the מתוך principle only covers things that all people do or need. Incense is used only by people with fancy tastes, so it stays forbidden. Marital relations are common to everyone, so a first בעילה is allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'About your point, the פסוק says': a פסוק answers your question
Something that is the same for every person, that everyone uses

phrases.english: He said to him: About your point, the verse said:
"Only what is eaten by every person"
a thing that is equal for every person.
phrases.notes: Incense is only for people with fancy tastes, while marital relations are something everyone has.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ עָלֶיךָ אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the incense challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the principle using a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מתוך principle allows any act without a need, so incense would be allowed too.
steps.terutzMaskana: מתוך covers only things equal for every person. Incense is not one of them; a first בעילה is.

steps.title: What about a deer, which not everyone has?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges רב אשי: deer is not food everyone has. Would that mean you cannot slaughter it on יום טוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: But if so, if a deer came his way on יום טוב, since it is not equal for every person, would it also be forbidden to slaughter it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge tests the 'equal for every person' rule from step 11 against a case that is clearly allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Deer meat is rare, and most people never get it. If the rule means 'something everyone actually has,' then slaughtering a deer on יום טוב would be forbidden. That is obviously wrong, so the rule seems too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: It happened to come his way
'Would it also be so?': asks whether we would really say that

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, נִזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ צְבִי בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: But if so, if a deer happened to come to him on יום טוב,
since it is not equal for every person,
would it also be forbidden to slaughter it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only things 'equal for every person' are allowed on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Deer is not available to everyone, so the rule would forbid slaughtering it, which is clearly wrong.

steps.title: The rule is about what everyone needs, not what everyone has
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that he meant something every person needs or would want. Deer meat is wanted by everyone, even if it is hard to get.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I was talking about something needed by every person. A deer is something needed by every person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי sharpens the rule so the deer is included and incense is still left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is not whether everyone actually owns the thing. The test is whether it is the kind of thing every person needs or would use. Everyone would eat deer if they had it, but only fancy people use incense even when it is available.
steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, the extension of permitted מלאכה covers only things that every person needs, like food or marital relations. Luxuries for a few people, like incense, stay forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא דְּבַר (הַ)צוֹרֶךְ לְכׇל נֶפֶשׁ קָאָמֵינָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: I was speaking of a matter that is a need for every person,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the little word ה here and some leave it out. Either way he means 'something everyone needs.'

phrases.english: and a deer is something needed by every person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֲנָא דְּבַר הַצוֹרֶךְ לְכׇל נֶפֶשׁ קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the deer challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Equal for every person' means something everyone actually has, so a rare deer would be left out.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means something every person needs or would want. Deer qualifies; incense does not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן ruled in צידן: no first בעילה on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי reports that רבי יוחנן ruled in the city of צידן that a first בעילה on שבת is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי said: רבי יוחנן ruled in צידן: it is forbidden to have a first בעילה on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי יוחנן that forbids a first בעילה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling goes against רבי אמי and רב זביד, who allowed it on שבת (steps 3-6). It fits רב פפא's version, which forbids it on שבת. The word 'הורה' (he ruled) will be questioned next.

keyTerms.meaning: צידן, a city where רבי יוחנן gave this ruling
To have a first בעילה with a new wife who is a בתולה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said:
Rabbi Yochanan ruled in Tzaidan:
It is forbidden to have a first בעילה on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי הוֹרָה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּצַיְידָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new opinion on the main question of first בעילה on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A first בעילה on שבת is forbidden.

steps.title: Can a stringent ruling be called a 'הוראה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording: is a stringent ruling something you would describe as 'הורה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there such a thing as a 'ruling' to forbid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning the word 'הורה' in רבי יעקב בר אידי's report. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling something a 'הוראה' suggests a firm, clearly known ruling. That word fits a lenient ruling, which needs clear backing. A stringent ruling can be given even out of doubt, so why call it a 'הוראה'?

keyTerms.meaning: A ruling that forbids, a stringent ruling

phrases.english: And is there such a thing as a 'ruling' to forbid?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא הוֹרָאָה לְאִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the report in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'הורה' used for רבי יוחנן's stringent ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'הוראה' suggests a firm ruling, which fits a lenient ruling. A stringent ruling can be given even when one is unsure, so the word seems out of place.

steps.title: Yes, 'הוֹרָה' is used for strict rulings too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'הוֹרָה' can describe a strict ruling, and brings a משנה where בית הלל 'ruled' that a woman must keep נזירות for seven more years.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Didn't we learn in a משנה: בית הלל ruled for her that she must be a נְזִירָה for another seven years?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. It brings a משנה where 'הוֹרוּהָ' describes a strict ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 suggested that 'הוֹרָה' is only used for lenient rulings. Here בית הלל 'ruled' something that made things harder for her: seven more years of נזירות. So the word clearly fits strict rulings as well, and רבי יוחנן's 'הוֹרָה ... אָסוּר' is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: And didn't we learn in a משנה?
A woman who took a vow of נזירות

phrases.english: Yes, and didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
Beit Hillel ruled for her
phrases.notes: 'Her' is Queen הילני from a משנה in נזיר. She had already kept seven years of נזירות outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: that she should be a nazirite
for another seven more years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15's question about the word 'הוֹרָה'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from usage that the word fits strict rulings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הוֹרָה' is only used for lenient rulings
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הוֹרָה' is also used for strict rulings, as with בית הלל and the queen

steps.title: A second proof: רבי ruled strictly like רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: Another proof from a ברייתא: רבי 'ruled' like רבי יעקב, who is stricter about a damaged spinal cord.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, like that which was taught in a ברייתא: a spinal cord that was cut through most of its width makes the animal a טריפה. These are the words of רבי. רבי יעקב says: even if it was only pierced. רבי ruled like רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second example where 'הוֹרָה' is used for a strict ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב makes the animal a טריפה even with only a hole in the spinal cord, which is stricter than רבי. The ברייתא says רבי 'הוֹרָה' like רבי יעקב. So again 'הוֹרָה' describes a strict ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut through most of its width

phrases.english: And alternatively, like that which was taught in a baraita:
A spinal cord that was severed for most of it
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Yaakov says: even if it was only pierced.
Rabbi ruled like Rabbi Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי, כִּי הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second proof for the answer in step 16
steps.raayaObject: That 'הוֹרָה' can describe a strict ruling
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a damaged spinal cord, where רבי 'ruled' like the stricter רבי יעקב

steps.title: רב הונא: the הלכה is not like רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that, even though רבי ruled like רבי יעקב, the הלכה does not follow רבי יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The הלכה is not like רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side ruling on the ברייתא just quoted. רב הונא decides the practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רבי himself ruled like רבי יעקב, רב הונא says the final הלכה is not like him. So a spinal cord that is only pierced does not make the animal a טריפה. This does not weaken the proof about the word 'הוֹרָה'.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law is not like this opinion

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The halacha is not like Rabbi Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the practical ruling on the ברייתא from step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a spinal cord cut through most of its width makes the animal a טריפה; a hole alone does not

steps.title: Another version: רבי יוחנן was asked and said it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches רבי יוחנן's ruling differently: it was an answer to a question asked in ציידן, and he answered 'forbidden'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches it this way. רבי אבהו said: רבי ישמעאל בן יעקב from צור asked רבי יוחנן in ציידן, and I heard it: What is the law about a first בעילה on שבת? He answered him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the story from step 14. In this version the ruling was an answer to a direct question, not a 'הוֹרָה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the word 'הוֹרָה' never appears, so the question from step 15 does not come up. The ruling itself is the same: רבי יוחנן forbade a first בעילה on שבת. רבי אבהו says he heard it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way (a different version)
To have a first בעילה with a בתולה

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak teaches it like this:
Rabbi Abahu said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן יַעֲקֹב דְּמִן צוּר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael ben Yaakov, from Tzor, asked
Rabbi Yochanan in Tzaidan,
and I heard it:
What is the law about a first intercourse on Shabbat?
And he said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of step 14 in which the wording problem of step 15 never comes up
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן, when asked, forbade a first בעילה on שבת

steps.title: Final ruling: a first בעילה on שבת is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules against רבי יוחנן: it is permitted to have a first בעילה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: it is permitted to have a first בעילה on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the whole discussion about a first בעילה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רבי יוחנן forbade it in both versions, the הלכה follows those who permit it: רבי אמי, רב זביד, and רב פפי's version of רבא. It rejects רבי יוחנן and רב פפא's version of רבא, which forbade it on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a first בעילה on שבת is permitted, even though רבי יוחנן forbade it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long sugya about whether a first בעילה on שבת or יום טוב is a problem, with a clear practical ruling.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
It is permitted to have a first intercourse on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: מוּתָּר לִבְעוֹל בַּתְּחִלָּה בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules against רבי יוחנן's view from steps 14 and 19
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A first בעילה on שבת is permitted

steps.title: Both a בתולה and an אלמנה need a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted through רב הונא, rules that a wedding needs the ברכה whether the bride is a בתולה or an אלמנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said that רב הונא said that רבי אבא בר זבדא said that רב said: both a בתולה and an אלמנה require a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the wedding ברכה. רב says it is said for every bride, even an אלמנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the ברכה is only for a first marriage of a בתולה. רב says no: an אלמנה's wedding needs it too. Notice that רב הונא is in the chain of names, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said that Rav Huna said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said that Rav said:
Both a virgin and a widow
require a blessing.
phrases.notes: This is the ברכת חתנים, the special wedding blessing said for the couple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the שבת discussion ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wedding ברכה is said for both a בתולה and an אלמנה

steps.title: Did רב הונא really say that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב הונא said elsewhere that an אלמנה does not need a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב הונא really say this? But didn't רב הונא say: an אלמנה does not require a ברכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 21 by setting it against another statement of רב הונא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, רב הונא passes on a ruling that an אלמנה needs a ברכה. Elsewhere he says she does not. The same person cannot hold both, so the גמרא asks how to fit them together.

phrases.english: But did Rav Huna really say this?
But didn't Rav Huna say:
A widow does not require a blessing!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's report that an אלמנה needs a ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A contradiction between two statements of the same אמורא

steps.title: Bachelor versus widower
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction: a bachelor who marries an אלמנה says the ברכה; a widower who marries an אלמנה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is a bachelor who married an אלמנה; there it is a widower who married an אלמנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each statement of רב הונא is about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether the ברכה is said depends on the groom too, not just the bride. If the groom was never married, an אלמנה bride still gets the ברכה. If both were married before, no ברכה is said.
steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא splits the cases: a בחור marrying an אלמנה gets the ברכה, and an אלמון marrying an אלמנה does not. Step 25 refines this: the אלמון still gets one day of ברכה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברכה depends only on the bride. Here the groom's status decides it.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, with a bachelor who married a widow,
there, with a widower who married a widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּבָחוּר שֶׁנָּשָׂא אַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by the groom's status)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's two statements about an אלמנה contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: A בחור marrying an אלמנה says the ברכה; an אלמון marrying an אלמנה does not

steps.title: Challenge from בועז, a widower who married a widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how an אלמון who marries an אלמנה could skip the ברכה, since בועז was exactly that case and he gathered ten men for the ברכת חתנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a widower who marries a widow really not say the ברכה? רב נחמן said in the name of הונא בר נתן that the ten-man requirement for ברכת חתנים comes from בועז gathering ten elders. And בועז was a widower marrying a widow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 23, which said a widower marrying a widow does not say the ברכה. It brings בועז as a counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for having ten men at ברכת חתנים is בועז's wedding to רות. בועז was an אלמון and רות was an אלמנה. So that case clearly had a ברכה, which seems to contradict Step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing said for a groom at a wedding
With a group of ten men

phrases.english: And a widower who married a widow does not [say the blessing]?
But didn't Rav Nachman say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן, תָּנָא:
phrases.english: Huna bar Natan said to me, it was taught:
From where do we know that the grooms' blessing is said with ten?
As it says:
"And he took ten men of the elders of the city
and said: Sit here, and they sat."
phrases.notes: רות 4:2. This is בועז gathering the elders when he married רות.

phrases.english: And Boaz was a widower who married a widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַלְמוֹן שֶׁנָּשָׂא אַלְמָנָה לָא? וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an אלמון who marries an אלמנה does not say the ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source for the ten-man ברכת חתנים is בועז, who was an אלמון marrying an אלמנה. So that case does have a ברכה.

steps.title: No ברכה for seven days, but yes for one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב הונא only meant the widow does not get the ברכה all seven days. For one day she does get it, which fits בועז.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did רב הונא mean by 'she does not need a ברכה'? He meant she doesn't need it for all seven days, but for one day she does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רב הונא's words more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No ברכה' does not mean zero ברכה. It means no seven-day ברכה like a regular wedding. For one day the ברכה is said, so בועז's ברכה with ten men fits fine.

keyTerms.meaning: She does not need a blessing
All seven days of the wedding celebration

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'אינה טעונה ברכה' as 'no ברכה at all'. After this answer, it means 'not for the full seven days'. One day of ברכה still applies.

phrases.english: What does "she does not need a blessing" mean,
that Rav Huna said?
She does not need a blessing all seven days,
but for one day she does need a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה בְּרָכָה דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from בועז in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the earlier statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא meant an אלמון who marries an אלמנה says no ברכה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant no ברכה for seven days. There is a ברכה for one day, as with בועז.

steps.title: A ברייתא about three days of rejoicing fits neither case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the Sages made sure the groom rejoices with the widow for three days. But a בחור has seven days and an אלמון has one, so which case does three days describe?
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the ברייתא that says the Sages took care of Jewish women so the groom would rejoice with her three days? Which case is that? If a bachelor, you said seven days! If a widower, you said one day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a third number, three days, that seems to clash with both the seven days and the one day it has just set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far: a בחור marrying an אלמנה gets seven days, and an אלמון marrying an אלמנה gets one day. The ברייתא speaks of three days for a widow, and three doesn't match either case.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages were careful and diligent

phrases.english: But what about that which was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁקְדוּ חֲכָמִים עַל תַּקָּנַת בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: The Sages were careful about the well-being of Jewish women,
that he should rejoice with her for three days.
phrases.notes: This is about a widow, who is married on Thursday so the celebration can last three days.

phrases.english: In which case?
If with a bachelor, didn't you say seven!
If with a widower, didn't you say one day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty against the seven-day and one-day system set up in Steps 23 and 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The division into seven days for a בחור and one day for an אלמון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives three days of rejoicing for a widow, which matches neither seven nor one.

steps.title: First answer: a widower has one day of ברכה but three days of שמחה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about an אלמון. He says the ברכה for one day, but rejoices with her for three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is about a widower: one day for the ברכה, and three days for rejoicing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: days of ברכה and days of rejoicing are two separate counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'one day' we said for an אלמון is only for the ברכה. The ברייתא's 'three days' is about rejoicing. So both numbers are true together for the אלמון.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces a possible answer)

phrases.english: If you want, say: with a widower,
one day for the blessing,
and three for rejoicing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּאַלְמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the challenge in Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting two separate counts: days of ברכה and days of שמחה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The one day for an אלמון covers everything, so three days of rejoicing can't fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: For an אלמון the ברכה is one day, but the rejoicing is three days.

steps.title: Second answer: a bachelor has seven days of ברכה but three days of שמחה
steps.stepSummary: Or the ברייתא is about a בחור marrying an אלמנה. He says the ברכה for seven days, but the special rejoicing lasts three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is about a bachelor: seven days for the ברכה, and three days for rejoicing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to fit the ברייתא, this time placing it with a בחור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the trick is that ברכה and rejoicing are counted separately. A בחור marrying an אלמנה says the ברכה for seven days, while the rejoicing the Sages made sure of is three days.
steps.whatToRemember: An אלמנה's wedding always has at least one day of ברכה. A בחור marrying her has seven days of ברכה, and an אלמון has one. The three days of rejoicing in the ברייתא are a separate count from the days of ברכה, and the גמרא offers two ways to place them.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: with a bachelor,
seven for the blessing,
and three for rejoicing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּבָחוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to the challenge in Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting two separate counts, applied to a בחור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A בחור has seven days, so three days can't describe his case.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a בחור the ברכה is seven days, while the rejoicing is three days.
